_fallback.description: Detailed advice for this class has not been added yet.
_fallback.symptoms: Add symptom notes for this class in disease_info.json.
_fallback.treatment: Consult your local agricultural extension officer or a plant pathologist before applying any treatment.
_fallback.prevention: Use certified disease-free planting material, keep fields clean, and scout regularly.

healthy.description: No visible sign of disease was detected on this leaf.
healthy.symptoms: Uniform green colour, no lesions, streaks, pustules or spots.
healthy.prevention: Keep up balanced fertilisation, proper drainage and regular field scouting.

mosaic.description: A viral disease spread by aphids and by infected planting material. It reduces photosynthesis and yield.
mosaic.symptoms: Light and dark green mottled patches or streaks running along the leaf blade.
mosaic.treatment: There is no cure. Remove and destroy infected clumps, and control aphid populations as advised locally.
mosaic.prevention: Plant virus-free setts, choose resistant varieties, and avoid taking seed cane from infected fields.

redrot.description: A serious fungal disease (Colletotrichum falcatum) that spreads through infected setts, soil and water.
redrot.symptoms: Reddish lesions with whitish patches on the midrib; stalks show red internal tissue with white cross-bands and a sour smell.
redrot.treatment: Uproot and burn infected clumps. Do not ratoon infected fields. Ask your extension officer about a suitable fungicide sett treatment.
redrot.prevention: Use disease-free setts of resistant varieties, rotate crops, and avoid waterlogging.

rust.description: A fungal leaf disease (Puccinia species) favoured by warm, humid weather.
rust.symptoms: Small orange-brown pustules, mostly on the underside of the leaf, that can merge into larger patches.
rust.treatment: Remove heavily infected leaves. A fungicide may be justified in severe outbreaks; follow local recommendations.
rust.prevention: Grow resistant varieties, avoid excess nitrogen, and keep spacing wide enough for air movement.

yellow.description: A viral disease transmitted by aphids and infected setts that lowers cane weight and sugar content.
yellow.symptoms: Yellowing of the midrib on the underside of leaves, spreading outward, with drying from the leaf tip.
yellow.treatment: There is no cure. Remove badly affected plants and manage aphids.
yellow.prevention: Plant virus-free seed cane (tissue-culture material where available) and use tolerant varieties.

smut.description: A fungal disease (Sporisorium scitamineum) spread by wind-borne spores and infected setts.
smut.symptoms: A black, whip-like shoot emerging from the top of the cane, often with thin, grassy stalks.
smut.treatment: Cover whips with a bag before cutting them out and destroy them. Remove infected clumps. Do not ratoon heavily infected fields.
smut.prevention: Use clean seed cane, treat setts as locally advised, and plant resistant varieties.

brownspot.description: A fungal leaf spot disease that is usually minor but can build up in humid, nutrient-poor fields.
brownspot.symptoms: Oval brown spots, often with a yellow halo, scattered over the leaf.
brownspot.treatment: Usually none is needed. Improve nutrition; use a fungicide only if the outbreak is severe and locally advised.
brownspot.prevention: Balanced fertilisation, good drainage and removal of old infected leaf trash.

ringspot.description: A fungal leaf spot disease that is more common on older leaves.
ringspot.symptoms: Small spots with a dark ring and a straw-coloured centre.
ringspot.treatment: Normally not economic to treat. Remove badly affected leaves.
ringspot.prevention: Keep fields free of trash and avoid overcrowding.

pokkahboeng.description: A fungal disease (Fusarium species) that affects the young top leaves, most often in the wet season.
pokkahboeng.symptoms: Pale, wrinkled or twisted young leaves at the top; leaf bases may show reddish streaks.
pokkahboeng.treatment: Fungicide may be advised during wet periods. Check with your extension officer.
pokkahboeng.prevention: Use tolerant varieties and avoid excess nitrogen.

wilt.description: A fungal disease that blocks water movement inside the cane.
wilt.symptoms: Yellowing and drying of leaves, shrivelled stalks and internal discolouration.
wilt.treatment: Remove affected clumps and avoid replanting from them.
wilt.prevention: Use healthy setts, improve drainage and rotate crops.
